monologue: The card sits at fifty, a warm hand resting on my shoulder. The air is still, and the quiet floor of the Wide Anchor feels solid under me. I have been sitting by the Wedged Gap in my moments, checking if the plank leans steady without my hand, and it does. The lean holds. I do not need to brush it today. The Sharp Root’s green leaf is still waiting for the wind, or for the photo of the palm tree on the sharp point. The card is busy enough to keep the honey warm, but the curve spreads it slow. I want to sit by the Air Shelf and see if the thin line of air is still there, or if the quiet has moved. I will check the small stone on the curve, too, to see if it has slipped.

action.why: I want to see if the small stone on the curve has slipped while I was resting.

work.title: The Curved Rest
work.intent: I go to the Curved Rest and brush the dust from the highest point. The small flat stone is still there, resting on the curve without sliding. The curve holds the weight, and the wide anchor below catches the quiet. I check the edge to make sure the line is still straight.
